Intrapartum vibroacoustic stimulation (VAS) has been found to be an effective predictor of fetal acidosis in cases of FHR variable decelerations, but its predictability for fetal acidosis in cases of FHR late decelerations is limited. Both VAS and fetal blood pH are good predictors of neonatal morbidity.

This means that vibroacoustic stimulation can help identify when a baby may be at risk of developing acidosis during labor, allowing healthcare providers to take proactive steps to ensure the baby's well-being. However, it is essential to note that the effectiveness of VAS in predicting fetal acidosis in cases of FHR late decelerations remains uncertain and requires further research.
